title: Context Has a Price: Adding and Removing Context for LLM Coding Agents under Prefix Caching
trick: Bill agent runs as uncached plus discounted cached input plus output; deleting an old tool output re-bills the whole suffix once, so observation masking that saves 19-25% undiscounted costs 87-116% more at a tenth-price cache.
framing_stripped: Called 'a measurement problem' with 'price-vector accounting', 'own-cache accounting', 'break-even masking' and a 'fixed-action replay'; it is the linear bill $U + cC + pO$ applied to the logged token streams of more than 20,000 vLLM runs of seven open models on SWE-bench, SWE-bench Verified and Loc-Bench under two main scaffolds (a minimal bash agent and mini-SWE-agent, with SWE-agent as a third), plus one observation about prefix caches: editing the prompt at a point invalidates the cached prefix for everything after that point, so the suffix is paid once more at the uncached price. That observation is written as the inequality $R\,c\,B > (1-c)\,S$ and used three ways: to explain why the keep-ten observation masking of Lindenbauer et al. flips from saving 19-25% at $c=1$ to costing 87-116% more at $c=0.1$ (Table 2); as a policy (MAR) that masks only when the inequality holds; and as a replay of the unmasked run under each rule that splits a method's premium into the cache-break term and the agent's extra steps (Table 6). The same bill applied to adding context shows a retrieved evidence package cuts read and search commands 18-34% but costs 33-42% more at $c=0.1$ with no established resolution gain (Table 4), and a methodological finding that sibling conditions run concurrently on one server warm each other's caches (Verified package premium $+8\%$ server-reported vs $+36\%$ own-cache, sec. 2).
method_equations: Cost model (sec. 1-2, Equation 1). For a run with requests $t = 1, \dots, T$, let $P_t$ be the prompt tokens of request $t$, $H_t \leq P_t$ the prompt tokens served from the prefix cache, and $O_t$ the output tokens. The three streams are $$U = \sum_t (P_t - H_t), \qquad C = \sum_t H_t, \qquad O = \sum_t O_t,$$ and the bill is $$\mathrm{cost}(c, p) = U + c\,C + p\,O,$$ where $c$ is the price of a cached input token and $p$ the price of an output token, both relative to an uncached input token (price 1). Main settings $c \in \{0.1, 1\}$, $p = 4$; grid in App. P $c \in \{0.025, 0.05, 0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1\}$, $p \in \{2, 4, 6, 8\}$; the 'current API range' is $0.025 \leq c \leq 0.1$, $4 \leq p \leq 6$ (sec. 2, App. J), citing Anthropic and OpenAI price lists accessed 2026-10-22 (cache read 0.025-0.1 of uncached, output 5-6x). Output is 19-38% of run cost at $c = 0.1$; the cached share of the bill is 18-30% at $c = 0.025$ and 90-95% at $c = 1$ (sec. 2). Own-cache accounting (sec. 2, App. K): $H_t = \min(P_t, \mathrm{LCP}_t)$ where $\mathrm{LCP}_t$ is the longest common token prefix of request $t$ and request $t-1$ of the same run, computed with the serving model's tokenizer; this counts reuse of the previous prompt only and 'does not model expiration or eviction'. Where token ids were not recorded, $H_t = \min(\hat H_t, P_{t-1})$ with $\hat H_t$ the server-reported hit count, which counts 9.8% fewer hits than the token count for Qwen3.6-27B (784-token vLLM blocks) and 0.8% fewer for Qwen3-Coder. Server-reported hits also include prefixes warmed by sibling conditions of the same task running concurrently (3.7-6.7% of prompt tokens in the affected conditions, none in the baseline), which moved the Verified package premium at $c = 0.1$ from $+8\%$ to $+36\%$ once removed; run alone on a fresh server, $+29\%$ (sec. 2, App. A, App. K). A 25% surcharge on cache writes was also tried: 'conclusions do not change' (App. K). Break-even rule (sec. 2, Equation 2). Removing $B$ tokens before request $t$ saves $c\,B$ on each of the $R$ remaining requests; the $S$ tokens of the prompt after the change point lose their cache hit once and cost an extra $(1-c)$ each. Removal pays when $$R\,c\,B > (1-c)\,S.$$ What is recomputed is the suffix $S$ after the edit, not the removed tokens and not the whole prompt; the first version of the analysis 'counted the removed tokens themselves as recomputed at the trigger (a median of about 18.6K instead of 4.5K tokens on Verified)' and was corrected (App. A). In App. K the recomputed amount $X$ at the request after removal is measured as its uncached tokens minus the median uncached tokens of the run's ordinary requests; $B$ is the removed tokens minus the tokens of the index that replaces them; $R$ is the remaining requests, actual in hindsight or the condition's median for the ex-ante rule. Worked example (Figure 2): $B = 1{,}000$, $S = 5{,}000$, $c = 0.1$; ten remaining requests save $1{,}000$ units and incur $4{,}500$ to rebuild the suffix; break-even needs $R = 45$. At $c = 1$ the rule favours removal whenever $R > 0$ and $B > 0$; at $c = 0.1$ it favours 'removing large blocks early and leaving small or late ones'. Adding context is the mirror image: $B$ added tokens cost at least $c\,B$ on every later request. Policy MAR (sec. 5): mask every unmasked observation outside the latest ten whenever Equation 2 holds, with $B$ and $S$ read from the current prompt and $$R = \min\bigl(250 - t,\ \max(59 - t,\ 25)\bigr)$$ estimated from a pilot's remaining-step distribution (mini-SWE-agent, 250-step cap); for GLM the estimate used $L = 167$ (App. I). First-order crossover for rolling masking (App. I, Equation 3): each turn removes one observation of about $o$ tokens and keeps the latest $K$ turns, so about $S \approx K(o + a)$ tokens are recomputed, $a$ the reply length; removal pays when $c\,o\,R > (1-c)\,K(o + a)$, and the crossover cache price is $$c^{\ast} \approx \Bigl(1 + \frac{\bar R}{K\,(1 + a/o)}\Bigr)^{-1},$$ with $\bar R$ the mean requests remaining when an observation is removed. Predicted 0.36 / 0.50 / 0.19 for Qwen3.6-27B / Qwen3-Coder / Qwen3.8-27B; measured (exact from linearity in $c$) 0.55 / 0.47 / 0.38; GLM 0.21 (estimate 0.15), Gemma 0.36 (estimate 0.19). Fixed-action replay (sec. 5, App. J). $K(g, \tau)$ is the cost of trajectory $\tau$ rendered under masking rule $g$; with $\tau_0$ the unmasked and $\tau_1$ the masked run of a task, $$\text{direct} = K(1, \tau_0) - K(0, \tau_0), \qquad \text{behavioral} = K(1, \tau_1) - K(1, \tau_0),$$ an accounting identity, not a causal mediation. Replay reproduces logged prompt length and own-cache prefix for 99.6-100% of requests. Table 6 ($c = 0.1$, total / direct / behavior / extra steps): mini-SWE-agent Qwen3.6-27B rolling $+116\% / +90\% / +26\% / +5.3$, batched $+4.9\% / -3.4\% / +8.2\% / +2.9$, break-even $+2.8\% / -3.7\% / +6.5\% / +2.7$; Coder rolling $+87\% / +86\% / +1.2\% / -0.1$; SWE-agent (115 tasks) rolling $+101\% / +52\% / +49\% / +23.7$, batched $+24\% / -21\% / +45\% / +23.2$, break-even $+9.6\% / -15\% / +25\% / +23.4$; with a step charge added to the rule $+4.3\% / -18\% / +22\% / +15.9$ (78 tasks). Headline tables. Table 2 (201 fresh Verified tasks, mini-SWE-agent, one run per cell, cost relative to no management MR, $c = 0.1$ / $c = 1$): Qwen3.6-27B rolling MM10 $+116\% / -19\%$, batched MB $+5\% / -22\%$, break-even MAR $+3\% / -26\%$, summarization MS $+22\% / -14\%$, AgentDiet-style MD $+36\% / +4\%$; Qwen3-Coder $+87 / -25$, $+12 / -4$, $+2 / -21$, $+28 / +3$, $+31 / +7$; Qwen3.8-27B $+76 / -24$, $-14 / -33$, $+7 / -21$, $-19 / -53$, $+29 / +2$; MR mean cost (thousands of cost units) 149 / 901, 69 / 347, 129 / 912. Kendall's $\tau$ between cost rankings at $c = 0.1$ and $c = 1$: $+0.20$, $+0.07$, $+0.47$. Table 4 (evidence package E5 minus no evidence E0, paired means; read+search / cost $c = 0.1$ / cost $c = 1$): SWE-bench test Qwen3.6-27B $-5.97 / +42\% / +33\%$; Verified Qwen3.6-27B $-6.64 / +36\% / +25\%$; Loc-Bench $-4.52 / +36\% / +28\%$; SWE-bench test Qwen3-Coder $-2.97 / +95\% / +68\%$; Verified 219 fresh $-4.87 / +42\% / +29\%$; mini-SWE-agent $-1.29 / +27\%$. Keeping the package to the end (E2) $+80\%$ to $+127\%$; by Equation 2 replacing the package with its index pays in 91-97% of runs at $c = 0.1$. Resolution: $-1.9$ pp on SWE-bench test, $+3.8$ on Verified (13 better, 10 worse), $+0.0$ on 217 fresh Verified tasks within the preregistered $\pm 5$ pp (sec. 4). Price-range test (App. J, P): cost differences are linear in $c$ and $p$, so a method is cheaper throughout the current range iff cheaper at its four corners; 'none of the 33 combinations we ran was'. Protocol (sec. 3): unit of analysis the task; runs averaged within task, conditions paired by task; 95% CIs from 2,000 bootstrap resamples over tasks; one-sided directional tests Holm-corrected within an experiment; non-inferiority margins preregistered in dated internal records.
load_bearing_assumption: That the own-cache previous-prompt token overlap, priced with a published reference vector, is the bill a user would pay: 'Prices are applied to recorded token streams rather than measured from API invoices' and the cache model 'does not model expiration or eviction' (sec. 2; Limitations). The sign flip rests on three things being true of a provider's cache: (i) a hit requires the previous prompt to be a token-exact prefix, so any edit at position $k$ re-bills the suffix at full price (vLLM semantics; the paper's own Qwen3-Coder server also reused the previous reply, which moves rolling masking from $+87\%$ to $+98\%$, App. K); (ii) the cache does not expire between an agent's turns, so $R$ remaining requests all hit; (iii) cache writes are free or cheap (a 25% surcharge was tested, App. K, and Anthropic's write price is not otherwise modelled). If a provider evicts within a run, charges writes at a premium, or caches at breakpoints rather than token prefixes, both $cB$ and $(1-c)S$ change and the measured crossovers (0.21-0.55) move. Second, that the agent's extra steps after masking are a property of masking rather than of these models and caps: the behavioral term is 'an accounting identity, not a causal mediation analysis', thinking is disabled, output is capped at 2,048 tokens per turn, and the extra-step cost is attributed from one run per cell at temperature 0.7.
weakest_component: The small-effect claims and the re-implemented baselines in Section 6, measured with one run per cell. The paper's own noise estimate is 'relative standard error of one evaluation's mean cost 3-4% (201 tasks, one run each); two evaluations differ by 4-5%' (Table 7), yet the paper reads break-even masking at $+2.8\%$ / $+1.8\%$ (Qwen3.6-27B / Coder), digests at $+2.4\%$ against no masking, batched masking at $+4.9\%$, and the 'within 7% of no management' ranking claim off single runs; the non-inferiority tests it preregistered at 5% fail for the Qwen models for exactly this reason. The LLM-summarization and AgentDiet arms use prompts the paper wrote itself because the originals are 'not public' (App. I), so 'summarization can flip too' and 'reflection with the agent's own model does not pay' are results about this paper's reconstructions. Next: the break-even controller's $R = \min(250 - t, \max(59 - t, 25))$ is a pilot heuristic, not a predictor, and the rule 'counts only the tokens it removes' while masked runs grew from 92 to 116 steps in SWE-agent; the quality scores use the working-tree diff, and 'submitted patches differ from working-tree patches in a quarter of runs' (Limitations), so every resolution delta of a few points is unverified; 'Each cell has one run' for Section 6 quality; the cache-hit measure is idealized (previous prompt only, no TTL, block granularity gives $+173\%$ instead of $+116\%$ for rolling masking); and all seven models are open models with thinking disabled, five from Qwen.
regime: Models: Qwen3.6-27B (main), Qwen3-Coder-30B-A3B, Qwen3.5-4B, Qwen3.5-9B, Qwen3.8-27B, Gemma-4-26B-A4B, GLM-4.7-Flash; all served locally with vLLM with prefix caching, at most eight concurrent runs per server; temperature 0.7, top-$p$ 0.8, at most 2,048 output tokens per turn, thinking disabled, seed fixed per task and repeat (sec. 3, App. B). Scaffolds: a minimal bash agent (one command per turn, at most 50 turns or 64K context; output beyond 6,000 characters keeps first and last 3,000), mini-SWE-agent 2.4.6 (250 steps in executable-sandbox experiments, 50 in the early evidence replication), SWE-agent 1.1.0 with function calling; Gemma used tool calls and a newer vLLM (App. A). Sandboxes: Linux namespaces, no network, no installed dependencies; an executable sandbox for Django 3.0-5.0 and SymPy where the gold patch passes on 293 of 304 Verified tasks. Benchmarks and sizes: 80 SWE-bench test tasks outside Verified; Verified with 219 fresh tasks for evidence and 201 for masking, 115 Django/SymPy tasks and 78 from seven other repositories; 224 Loc-Bench tasks (184 held out); 183 tasks for the evidence x execution cross; 178 tasks for App. G methods. More than 20,000 runs in total; 3,618 runs in the six-method re-evaluation; 27,389 requests audited for cache reuse; 13,330 prompts replayed in the digest confirmation. Horizon: GLM-4.7-Flash 171 steps per run on average with 21 of 115 unmasked runs hitting the 131K context limit; Gemma 103 steps; SWE-agent Qwen3.6-27B 92 steps unmasked, 116 masked; mini-SWE-agent runs with the package 20.4 vs 28.1 steps in the minimal agent; more than half of mini-SWE-agent runs hit the 50-step cap in the early replication. Cost scale: no-management mini-SWE-agent run costs 149K cost units at $c = 0.1$ and 901K at $c = 1$ for Qwen3.6-27B (Table 2); cache reads are 94-98% of input tokens, against 95.6% in 8,058 Claude Code and Codex sessions (sec. 2). Resolution bands: local 0.61-0.71 (Qwen3.6-27B), 0.26-0.32 (Qwen3-Coder), 0.66-0.75 (Qwen3.8-27B) on 115 executable tasks (App. I); Gemma official 0.109 with 62-64% empty patches (App. F); Qwen3.5-9B among submitted runs 0.43-0.44 (App. M). Prices: $c \in \{0.1, 1\}$ and $p = 4$ in the main text; grid in App. P. Code and data release: unknown (not in text). Venue: unknown (not in text); arXiv v1 17 Nov 2026, Huawei Technologies.
information_asymmetry: The run-time controller versus hindsight. At the moment a block is removed the controller 'can measure $B$ and $S$, but must estimate $R$' (sec. 2): how many requests remain, whether the masked content will be re-fetched (rolling masking adds 2.0 re-fetches and 5 steps per run for Qwen3.6-27B, 5.7 in SWE-agent), and whether the run will end at the context limit (GLM: 21 of 115 unmasked runs) all exist only after the run ends. The paper fills $R$ with a pilot median and, in one variant, charges each masked observation its expected share of the extra steps, which 'masked a third as often and cut the premium to $+4.3\%$' (App. I); the fixed-action replay reads the direct term off the logged trajectory in hindsight, where $R$ is known exactly. Second asymmetry, run versus server: a run's bill depends on what the server already holds. Sibling conditions of the same task warm each other's prefixes ($+8\% \to +36\%$), and in production 'Whether a prefix stays cached also depends on concurrent agents' (sec. 7); the run sees only its own prompts. What the 20,000-run measurement holds fixed: the price vector as a reference ($c \in [0.025, 0.1]$, $p \in [4, 6]$ from two price lists accessed 2026-10-22, 'not measurements of a provider's billing system'); the cache as the token-exact longest common prefix with the same run's previous prompt, so no TTL, no eviction, no breakpoints, no write charge beyond a 25% sensitivity, no cross-request reuse of the previous reply except as an audit; the serving stack as vLLM with 784-token blocks and at most eight concurrent runs; thinking disabled and output capped at 2,048 tokens per turn; step caps of 50 or 250; fixed seeds. What it cannot see: a provider's invoice; a provider's cache under load, where a long think between turns or a queue could evict the prefix and make every request uncached; wall-clock latency and sandbox compute ('We report inference-token cost, not total sandbox compute or wall-clock latency'); the causal effect of removal on the agent's actions, since 'a masked agent would not have taken the same actions'; the quality effect of any method to better than a few points, because the scored patch differs from the submitted patch in a quarter of runs; and the stopping decision, which 'affect[s] the same expensive tail of a run' and is deferred to companion work. Inference (not the paper's claim): the gap left open is a run-time estimator of $R$ and of re-fetch probability from the run's own state, a provider-billed replication of the sign flip on one closed model, and a joint stopping-and-removal controller; the paper's own controller with per-command-type reuse priors did not beat the break-even rule (App. F, G).
occupies: Published: that keep-ten rolling observation masking, the setting recommended by Lindenbauer et al., raises cost by 87-116% at a tenth-price cache and lowers it 19-25% without a discount for Qwen3.6-27B and Qwen3-Coder on 201 fresh Verified tasks in mini-SWE-agent (preregistered, Table 2), with the flip replicated in SWE-agent ($+101\% / -29\%$), GLM-4.7-Flash ($+38\% / -36\%$) and Gemma-4 ($+56\%$ at $c = 0.1$); the three-stream price-vector bill $U + cC + pO$ with own-cache token-level hit counting and the closed-form break-even inequality $R\,c\,B > (1-c)\,S$, used as the policy MAR; the fixed-action replay that splits a method's premium into a cache-break term and the agent's reaction (Table 6); that a retrieved evidence package cuts read and search commands 18-34% on every Qwen model and benchmark, random code of the same length does not, cost rises 33-42% at $c = 0.1$, and resolution is equivalent within $\pm 5$ pp on 217 fresh Verified tasks (sec. 4); that appending the retrieval ranking to the agent's localization answer raises function Acc@10 by 14-20 points for three models at no token cost; that six methods re-rank between $c = 0.1$ and $c = 1$ (Kendall's $\tau$ 0.07-0.47) and none of 33 method-model-scaffold combinations is cheaper than no management across the current API range; that concurrent sibling conditions share caches and bias cost ablations ($+8\%$ vs $+36\%$); the six-point measurement checklist of App. O; and that deterministic digests lower the break-even cache price to 0.03-0.13 and save 13-17% for GLM at $c = 0.1$.

neighbors.title: The Complexity Trap: Simple Observation Masking Is as Efficient as LLM Summarization for Agent Context Management
neighbors.trick: Replace old environment observations with a placeholder, keeping the latest few, and the SWE-agent bill halves relative to the raw agent while matching LLM summarization's solve rate on SWE-bench Verified across five model configurations (abstract fetched); cited here as 'Observation masking matches LLM summarization for SWE agents' and its keep-ten setting as 'the setting recommended by Lindenbauer et al. (2025)'; this paper shows that halving holds only at $c = 1$ and reverses to $+87$-$116\%$ at $c = 0.1$ because every turn rewrites the prefix.

neighbors.title: Token Reduction Is Not Cost Reduction
neighbors.trick: Run three token-reduction tools against an unmodified Claude Code baseline and bill them at provider prices: the largest setup removed 38.4% of tool-output tokens but raised billed cost 6.8%, token reduction correlates with cost reduction at Pearson $r = 0.15$, and cache creation and reads dominate input-side cost (abstract fetched); cited here as 'token reduction need not reduce cost' and 'Methods that reduce token counts can thus raise cost'; this paper replaces one provider's bill with a parametric price vector on open models, adds the closed-form break-even rule and the fixed-action decomposition, and scales to 20,000 runs.

neighbors.title: TokenPilot: Cache-Efficient Context Management for LLM Agents (Xu et al., Findings of EMNLP 2026)
neighbors.trick: Evict context by its remaining value in batches timed to keep the prefix cache intact; cited here as the method that 'evicts by remaining value in cache-friendly batches', and this paper's batched masking MB is 'close in spirit to batched eviction'; abstract not fetched (no arXiv id in the text), described from this paper's text only.

theme_fit.why: directly answers the lane sentence: compaction as a serving and cost lever under prefix caching, with the true cost structure of agentic workloads written as a three-stream bill, a cache-break inequality, a crossover price per model and scaffold, and the finding that no removal method beats doing nothing across the current API price range; the sibling-cache bias is a systems measurement result in its own right

the lossy messages the lane names (masking placeholders, LLM summaries, reflection rewrites, digests, retrieved evidence) are priced for what they cost in cache breaks and in the agent's extra steps, measured with a fixed-action replay; the lane's measurement register exactly, and the race window is open because the paper leaves the run-time estimator of remaining requests and re-fetch probability unbuilt

supplies an instrument and a bias catalogue for cost accounting (App. O checklist, Table 7: concurrent cache sharing, block-granular hits, previous-reply reuse, evaluation noise of 3-5% per evaluation) and a preregistration protocol with every unsupported test reported; cost per task is a lane hint, but the paper's object is the serving bill rather than agent evaluation at large
compaction appears as a training problem only in the narrow-read LoRA fine-tune (App. G) and the efficiency distillation (App. M), both supervised, both negative for quality; same words, no RL

limitations_as_complaints: I run seven open models with thinking off and step caps that many runs hit, so I cannot tell a team paying a frontier provider whether their masking flips sign at their cache price and reasoning budget: 'All models are open models served locally, and five of the seven are from the Qwen family. Our settings disable thinking where supported and use bounded output and step budgets; early evidence replications use a 50-step cap that many runs reach. These results do not establish how frontier API agents or longer reasoning budgets would behave' (Limitations).

My bill is a formula over logged token streams with an idealized cache, not an invoice, so a provider that expires prefixes between turns, charges cache writes or caches at breakpoints could move every crossover I report, and I never priced latency or the sandbox: 'Prices are applied to recorded token streams rather than measured from API invoices. The cache accounting approximates within-run reuse and does not reproduce provider-specific expiration, write charges, breakpoints or load-dependent eviction. We report inference-token cost, not total sandbox compute or wall-clock latency' (Limitations).

My break-even rule decides with the remaining requests guessed from a pilot and the agent's reaction assumed away, so it masks observations the agent then re-fetches and runs grow from 92 to 116 steps, 'a cost that the rule, which counts only the tokens it removes, does not see' (sec. 5); 'Break-even masking estimates remaining requests and holds behavior fixed in its calculation; it missed its cost non-inferiority margin for the Qwen models, although it passed for GLM' (Limitations).
